identity_evidence.quote: 17-year-old girl with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) nephritis

attribution_limitations: The Figure 1 caption describes the abdominal ultrasound finding as a 4.9 x 4.1 x 5 cm heterogeneous mass in the uterus, while the case text describes the ultrasound and CT finding as a 4.7 cm hemorrhagic right ovarian cyst.

The abstract says the hemorrhagic ovarian cyst resolved completely in 3 months, while the case text and Figure 1C describe a decreasing-sized or reduced lesion (<2 cm) at the same three-month point; the caption calls the study abdominal ultrasonography, the text pelvic ultrasonography. Both sides agree the lesion shrank; whether it persisted is in conflict.
The case text names deflazacort as the steroid she is currently taking, while the discussion names prednisolone.
The Figure 3 caption prints the menorrhagia start as December 2018.12; the case text places persistent menorrhagia three months after the visit and later intermittent menorrhagia.

Three months later, Since then and 5 days later are anchored only by the adjacent sentences; the visit date and the LAHPS diagnosis date are not stated, and the Figure 3 caption dates the cyst to December 2018.

A tingling sensation at the fingertips in June 2020 is mentioned in the discussion, and throbbing pain of finger tips is listed in the case text after the diagnosis; the source does not say whether these are the same symptom.

The discussion says laboratory criteria were satisfied and that development of vascular thrombosis and future pregnancy complications might be possible, and that she should be monitored for antiphospholipid syndrome; no antiphospholipid syndrome diagnosis is made.
Anti-factor II antibody could not be tested; the LAHPS diagnosis rests on recurrent bleeding, prolonged PT and aPTT, low prothrombin level and lupus anticoagulant positivity as the authors state.
The steroid named in the dose-increase sentence is not stated, and the case text does not say which steroid is meant by the abstract mention of glucocorticoids given with cyclophosphamide.

The case text says the laboratory abnormalities persisted without bleeding or thrombotic complications and the discussion says her bleeding symptoms were controlled, while another discussion sentence says recurrent bleeding events take place; the time of that statement is not given.
